answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake tied to verifiable work, like a cedar that only grows after seasons of care. Newcomers start on a small island of low-trust tasks, earning reputation slowly, while a shared meadow of public audit trails records every completed job and dispute. Creating fake identities then costs real stake plus time, and bad behavior burns the stake, so an attacker must pay far more than any single fraud can earn.
